subject: reactive tableOutput()s, using multiple tabPanel()s, is requiring multiple submitButton() clicks

messages.author: 57a95aa350db9768
messages.subject: reactive tableOutput()s, using multiple tabPanel()s, is requiring multiple submitButton() clicks
parts:
This is pseudo-code, but hopefully it will describe my problem:

---
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel('title'),
  sidebarPanel(),
  mainPanel(
    submitButton(),
    tabsetPanel(
      tabPanel('Table1',
        tableOutput('table1')
      ),
      tabPanel('Table2',
        tableOutput('table2')
      )
    )
  )
))

---
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  getTable <- reactive({
    myTable <- functionThatGeneratesTable()  # a data frame
    myTable
  })
  output$table1 <- renderTable({
    head(getTable())
  })
  output$table2 <- renderTable({
    head(getTable())
  })
})

... the result being that the tabPanel() that is selected when I click the submitButton() is the one that is updated. I would also like to have the unselected tabPanel() update itself without having to select it and click the submitButton() again. For example, if I have the 'Table1' tab selected and click the submitButton(), the reactive tableOutput('table1') updates as expected, but tableOutput('table2') does not... to update tableOutput('table2') I have to then select the 'Table2' tab and click the submitButton() again - doing this does not appear to run the getTable() calculations again, but rather just pulls an already evaluated table (which is nice), but it'd be great if the tables in the 'Table1' AND 'Table2' tabs would update simultaneously, without the need for the 2 extra clicks. I would suppose this is possible, and I just need an extra bit of code somewhere.

Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: reactive tableOutput()s, using multiple tabPanel()s, is requiring multiple submitButton() clicks
parts:
The submitButton in Shiny is problematic. I would suggest using actionButton from shiny-incubator. Here's an example app:
  http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/actionbutton/

Source code:
  https://gist.github.com/wch/4963887

That should probably be enough to get you going, but if you want to fully understand how it works, see the tutorial section on Isolation (and to fully understand that, you'll want to read all the sections in Understanding Reactivity).
  http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#isolation

-Winston
